builds.howItPlays: Early on you hold back with removal and cheap plays while you set up your rune engine, using Sivir's ability to turn recycled runes into gear tokens and to ready her whenever an enemy unit dies. Once you land your big finisher, usually a huge dragon or a wave of gear-powered attacks, you turn every one of those stored resources into a turn your opponent can't answer.
builds.whyYou: You like a deck that asks you to wait, build up a stash of resources, and then cash them all in at once. Patience appeals to you more than jumping out to an early lead, but you still want the payoff to feel enormous when it lands. This Legend suits you if you don't mind that some games fizzle before you get there, because the ones that go your way go big.
builds.ratingNotes: pace 4.5: riftbound.gg describes 'mid-range tempo, combining early defensive play with a late-game win condition.' stance 4.5: the same guide says the deck is 'primarily reactive early, becoming proactive late,' a matchup-dependent switch rather than a fixed lean. complexity 6.5: cardsrealm's Miracle Sivir piece says the list is 'only a low tier-1 or high tier-2 list in less experienced hands,' meaning the sequencing (discounting Rhasa the Sunderer, tracking Gold Gear Tokens) matters a lot. variance 7.5: the same article calls the deck 'very hit or miss - you can theoretically beat any deck in the meta, but you might as well lose too,' and warns some matchups give you 'only one chance to win.' Legend ability: when you recycle a rune you may exhaust Sivir to play a Gold gear token exhausted, and she readies whenever one or more enemy units die. Confidence: medium. The two sources describe two different Sivir shells (a dragon/control build and a faster Miracle/Rhasa build) rather than one agreed list, so these numbers average both; a reviewer familiar with the current meta should confirm which build is more representative today.
